pages.markdown:
# The junior pathway

Welcome to the junior pathway! This is your guide to how young golfers start, learn, and grow at our club. Whether you are a junior looking to try golf for the first time, or a parent with no golf experience, you'll find helpful information here. 

The pathway is designed to be simple, supportive, and fun. Juniors begin as Cadets, learning the basic skills, safety, and good habits. As they grow in confidence, they move on to become Course Cadets, playing more golf on the course, trying new challenges, and enjoying more independence.

Parents and families are very important in this journey, and we work together to make sure everyone feels happy and welcome. You do not need any special equipment or golf knowledge to get started, just enthusiasm and a willingness to learn. Let’s get started step by step!

pages.markdown:
# Cadet stage

The Cadet stage is where most juniors begin their golfing adventure. At this level, the focus is on having fun, making friends, and learning the basics of golf in a relaxed way. Lessons are playful and short, so everyone can enjoy themselves without feeling any pressure.

We teach simple skills like how to hold the club, how to stand, and how to swing safely. Cadets also learn how to behave on and around the golf course, such as waiting their turn, looking after the course, and being respectful to others. These habits help everyone have a good time.

There’s no need to buy fancy equipment. We have everything you need to get started and will help you choose suitable clubs and balls when you’re ready. Parents and families are encouraged to watch, support, and join in activities if they wish. The main aim is to build confidence and spark an interest in golf.

pages.markdown:
# Course Cadet stage

After becoming comfortable with the basics, juniors move up to the Course Cadet stage. Here, they start to play on real parts of the golf course, but still in a relaxed setting and with age-appropriate holes or distances.

Course Cadets practice playing a few holes at a time, learning how to move safely around the course and play as a team. They try different types of shots, work with others, and get a taste of what actual golf is like without any heavy competition.

Parents may walk along, offer gentle encouragement, or simply enjoy watching. Coaches are always nearby to offer support and tips. There’s still no need for expensive equipment – we’ll advise on any useful items as children grow. The aim is to build enjoyment, skills, and understanding of golf’s unique atmosphere.

pages.markdown:
# Expectations and support

Joining the junior golf pathway is not about being perfect – it’s about trying your best, being kind, and having a good time. Juniors are encouraged to listen, try new things, and respect other players. Little steps and small improvements matter much more than winning or looking ‘good’.

Parents don’t need to be experts. Your support and encouragement are what truly count. You might help juniors arrive on time, provide a bottle of water, or simply cheer them on from the side. If you have questions at any time, coaches or organisers are always happy to help. We welcome feedback and believe in working together with families.

Remember, safety and enjoyment come first. If a junior feels worried or unsure, let a coach know early. We aim for every child to feel welcome and secure, no matter how much experience they have.

pages.markdown:
# Meet the team

Behind every successful junior section is a team of caring people. Here at the club, your child will be supported by skilled coaches, friendly volunteers, and dedicated organisers. Our coaches are trained to teach children and know how to make golf enjoyable and safe.

Volunteers often help with activities, keep things running smoothly, and are there to answer practical questions. You may also meet older juniors who act as role models or ‘buddies’ to help new members settle in.

Everyone in our team aims to make the golfing experience welcoming for all families, no matter how much you know about golf. We encourage parents to introduce themselves and ask anything – we’re always here to help. Let’s enjoy golf together!

pages.markdown:
# Quick check

Let's review what we've learned about the junior golf pathway. Answer these questions to see how ready you are to support or start as a junior golfer.

questions.question: What is the main focus of the Cadet stage?

choices.text: Having fun, making friends, and learning basics

questions.explanation: The Cadet stage is about fun, friends, and learning basic golf skills.

questions.question: Do parents need to know about golf before their child joins?

choices.text: Yes, they must be golf experts
No, encouragement and support are enough
Only if they want to play themselves
Yes, they need to buy lots of equipment

questions.explanation: Parents just need to support and encourage; they don’t need to be golf experts.

questions.question: Who can you ask if you're unsure about something at the club?

choices.text: You must figure it out on your own

questions.explanation: You can always ask coaches, volunteers, or team members for help.

questions.question: What happens at the Course Cadet stage?

choices.text: Juniors start to play on the actual golf course in a relaxed way

questions.explanation: Course Cadets play on parts of the real course, learning at their own pace.

questions.question: What should you do if a junior feels worried?

choices.text: Speak to a coach or team member

questions.explanation: It’s important to talk to a coach or someone on the team if there are any worries.
